system.summary: Latin clear text with a two-part nomenclator of 3-4 digit groups (some with 1/2) and letter signs (Lq Rex Sueciae, aa cum, rr et, t in), and words spelled with numbers 10-99, three homophones per letter in consecutive blocks (15-17 s, 18-20 m, 21-23 f, 24-26 e, 27-29 l, 30-32 r, 36-38 x, 39-41 q, 45-47 d, 48-50 c, 51-53 i, 54-56 p, 57-59 w?, 60-62 u, 63-65 o, 66-68 h, 69-71 b, 72-74 a, 75-77 g, 78-80 n, 81-83 t); nulls 10, 11, 88-90, 95, 97-99.

prior_solution.where: Contemporary interlinear glosses on the glossed letters (existing). No decipherment on image 442 or its neighbours. No edition of these letters found (searches of 6 Nov 2026, catalogue row 2313 vetting n09); not on DECODE; no target for this volume in the repository (origin/main f6b285a7b, 13 Nov 2026). Not opened: F. H. Schubert, Ludwig Camerarius (1955) and Stålhane 1934 ('Camerarius key'); Riksarkivet Chifferklaver I:19 A and I:22 not digitised.

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout set the rules (pre-registration, frozen keys and transcriptions, one measurement per test, thresholds fixed in advance). AI agents transcribed, built the letter table and the code list, ran the tests and wrote up; a separate agent did the blind second transcription pass and another the blind judging. No human palaeographer checked the transcription.
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout

solution.what: Letter table learned from the glosses of images 409, 414, 423, 427, frozen.
Held-out image 498: 83 glossed letters, 0.904 against 0.277 for the best of 200 shuffled keys (thresholds 0.85 and +0.30).
Code groups and glosses of images 402, 405, 406, 412, 415, 418, 419 added to those of 414, 423, 427, 498: 109 groups (codes.tsv), frozen.

Held-out image 442 (unglossed), transcribed after the freeze in two passes: blind forced choice between the list's value and a random decoy for the 59 covered code occurrences, 59/59 against 0.695 for the best of 200 random controls (thresholds n >= 30, 0.85 and +0.30). 4 items had an empty filler by a clean-up flaw; without them 55/55 against 0.673.
Image 442 read with key.tsv and codes.tsv: 335 of 414 word units read by sense (0.81).

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: Letter table and code list learned from the contemporary glosses of other letters of the volume and validated on held-out letters (498, 442); then applied to the unglossed postscript 442.

validation.notes: Contributor's pre-registered held-out tests (not docs/_validate.py): letter table 0.904 vs 0.277 on image 498; code list 59/59 vs 0.695 (blind forced choice) on image 442.

credits.note: interlinear glosses on the glossed letters; the letter table and the code list were learned from them
glossed code groups (codes.tsv), letter table (key.tsv), held-out tests (validation.txt), image 442 transcribed and read in part (reading.md)

texts.label: image 442, Post script of 20/30 Sept 1630
texts.summary: Frederick Henry offers his help; Camerarius urges a diversion or Dutch support under the King of Sweden; the Prince defers to the States General; the Duke of Neuburg and Count Wilhelm's troops; Camerarius asks the King to send someone and warns of intrigues against him.

reading_review.note: Read by sense with the validated letter table and code list; one AI reader, no independent or human review; count by script (reading.md).
reading_review.by: Claude Opus 5.5 agent for Brice Dudout

outcome.notes: The glossed letters were deciphered at the time; what is new is the letter table and the code list as validated reusable tables, and a partial reading of the unglossed postscript 442.
